holidays.name: National Spaghetti Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to twirling, slurping, and splattering sauce on your shirt in honor of the world's most beloved long noodle. Pasta fans celebrate with everything from classic marinara to creative spaghetti-topped pizzas.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday that appeared in the early 2000s on food-observance calendars. It has no single known founder and grew through food bloggers, restaurants, and social media.
holidays.funFact: Spaghetti means 'little strings' in Italian. It is the plural of 'spaghetto', which comes from 'spago', meaning twine.

holidays.name: World Braille Day
holidays.description: A day recognizing the tactile writing system that opened up reading and writing for blind and visually impaired people. Events include Braille workshops, accessibility campaigns, and tributes to its inventor.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly officially established it in 2018, and it was first observed on January 4, 2019. The date is the birthday of Louis Braille, born in 1809 in Coupvray, France.
holidays.funFact: Louis Braille was only 15 when he developed his system in 1824. He based it on 'night writing', a military code of raised dots that soldiers could read in the dark.

holidays.name: Trivia Day
holidays.description: A day for nerds, quiz champions, and know-it-alls to share random facts, host pub quizzes, and win arguments with obscure knowledge. Bonus points for facts nobody asked for.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popularized by trivia lovers and promoted online, it is placed at the start of the year as a way to kick off fresh learning and fact collecting.
holidays.funFact: The word 'trivia' comes from the Latin 'trivium', meaning 'three roads' or a crossroads. It was where ordinary people met and shared everyday chatter.

holidays.name: National Bobblehead Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the adorable, wobbly-headed figurines that sit on desks, dashboards, and ballpark shelves everywhere. Collectors show off their nodding favorites, from sports stars to presidents and cartoon characters.
holidays.origin: Created by the National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, which has pushed for the holiday as part of its mission to celebrate bobbleheads. It falls in early January to kick off the new collecting year.
holidays.funFact: Bobbleheads date back to 18th-century Russia, where a nodding mandarin figure appeared in a story. Modern versions became widely popular after baseball teams began making them in the 1960s.

holidays.name: National Run Up the Stairs Day
holidays.description: An unofficial fitness-flavored observance that encourages people to ditch the elevator and sprint up the nearest staircase. It is a tongue-in-cheek way to burn off holiday cookies.
holidays.origin: It popped up on quirky holiday calendars as a New Year's resolution booster, inspired by the idea that January is the perfect time to start moving more.
holidays.funFact: Stair climbing burns more calories per minute than jogging on flat ground. Some cities host 'tower runs' where people race up skyscrapers with thousands of steps.
